Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter · 2 marks

steps.label: The definition
steps.mark_note: Stream of electrons from the cathode
lines: Cathode rays are a stream of electrons
coming from the cathode in a discharge tube.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the particle (electrons) and where the stream starts (the cathode).
steps.why: Cathode rays were named before anyone knew what they were. J. J. Thomson showed they are charged particles — electrons — so the definition names the particle, not just the glow.
common_mistakes: Calling cathode rays electromagnetic waves. They are moving electrons, with charge and mass.
Saying they come from the anode. They come from the cathode, the negative electrode.

recall.must_convey: That cathode rays are a stream of electrons coming from the cathode of a discharge tube.
reject: low pressure and high potential difference

steps.memory_tip: CAthode rays CArry Charge — they are electrons leaving the cathode.

steps.label: How they are produced
lines: They are produced in a discharge tube kept at
a low pressure of about 0.001 mm of mercury,
with a high potential difference of about

lines.text: Cathode rays: electrons from the cathode

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Give both conditions with their values: the low pressure and the high potential difference.
steps.why: At ordinary pressure the gas does not conduct. Only at a very low pressure with a high potential difference do electrons leave the cathode and cross the tube as a beam.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the two conditions. The low pressure and the high potential difference carry this mark.
Writing 0.001 mm of mercury as the potential or 10 kV as the pressure. Keep each value with its own quantity.

recall.must_convey: That cathode rays are produced in a discharge tube at a low pressure of about 0.001 mm of mercury with a high potential difference of about 10 kV.

steps.memory_tip: Two conditions, two values: pressure DOWN to 0.001 mm of Hg, potential UP to 10 kV.

insider_note: The two marks are the particle and the tube conditions — write electrons from the cathode, then 0.001 mm of mercury and 10 kV.
